precepts.text: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools. Some come into the sanctuary with pride and contention, thinking they know much when they do not; keep your foot means keep your mouth shut and hear, the same charge God gave Moses at the bush.
precepts.point: God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
At the bush God told Moses, “Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.” The Most High expects humility, that we humble ourselves before him. Moses was a great man in Egypt, second to Pharaoh, raised in all the customs of Egypt, and God said, I don't want to hear all of that. The shoes were symbolic.

Ecclesiastes 5:1 is what the Most High requires: “Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.” A lot of times we come with pride and contention, acting like we know. You don't know a damn thing, because if you did, you would not have followed white Jesus.

Our brothers and sisters in the world do not consider that they are in evil, and a lot of times when they come into the sanctuaries it is the same thing: pride, contention, thinking they know much when they do not. Keep thy foot means keep your mouth shut when you enter the house of God and be ready to hear, the same thing he told Moses.

The same is required of us coming into this truth. All the Christian garbage we learned, leave it outside. Islam, garbage, leave it outside. Nuwaubianism, Afrocentric, black power: all garbage. We must reform our minds as Israelites and meditate in these scriptures.

precepts.text: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
precepts.point: A vow to the Most High is not to be made lightly. When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; better not to vow than to vow and not pay. Jacob vowed and rolled with the Most High, and he paid his vow.

note.label: Genesis 28: The Charge and the Vow at Bethel

precepts.why:
Jacob “vowed a vow”: if God will be with him, keep him in the way, give him bread to eat and raiment to put on, and bring him again to his father’s house in peace, “then shall the Lord be my God”, the stone shall be God’s house, and “of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.”

A vow to the Most High is not to be made lightly. “When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.” Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before the angel that it was an error, “wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?”

Jacob vowed and rolled with the Most High, and he paid his vow.

precepts.text: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; the Most High sees the oppression.
precepts.point: He looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian and hid him in the sand. He did not just marvel at the oppression; he used his position for his people, unlike many who hold a position of power today and will not risk it for their people. Moses is the ultimate revolutionary, as Christ is.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

precepts.why:
“If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.” The Most High sees the oppression. Moses went out unto his brethren and looked on their burdens and saw an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren, and he that is higher than the highest regarded it too.

Moses knew the Israelites were his brothers. He knew he was not of the Egyptian lineage, that there was something different about him. And he did not just marvel at the oppression: he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian and hid him in the sand. He used his position for his people, unlike many who hold a position of power today and will not risk it for their people.

Moses is the ultimate revolutionary, as Christ is.

precepts.text: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God; the evil still in a man from the world will corrupt him as it did our forefathers.
precepts.point: Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation. Moses was of the tribe of Levi, of the seed of Jacob, so the Lord could have started over with him.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

precepts.why:
“Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.”

Not forty days gone, and Israel had already turned aside quickly out of the way, made a molten calf and worshipped it. The spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left. They considered not that they did evil; they thought they were giving a sacrifice.

It is the same coming into this truth. The evil carried in from the world will corrupt you and turn you from the Lord if it is not put off, as it did our forefathers. Without the laws of God we are a carnal, rebellious, stiffnecked people, so these last days call for humbleness and repentance, being more ready to hear, not bringing the world's rhetoric into the congregation.

precepts.text: Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin.
precepts.point: A man was held accountable for whatever came out of his mouth; pronouncing with his lips and not performing it was sin. When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it, for better is it that thou shouldest not vow than that thou shouldest vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin. Christ set the same standard on the mouth: let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
A man was held accountable for whatever came out of his mouth; pronouncing with his lips and not performing it was sin. “When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.”

“Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?” Brothers say, I swear to God; watch your mouth. The soul that swore and did not perform had to confess that he had sinned in that thing and bring his trespass offering.

precepts.text: Pay that which thou hast vowed; better not to vow than to vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin, neither say before the angel that it was an error.
precepts.point: If thou shalt forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee; but that which is gone out of thy lips thou shalt keep and perform. Do not suffer thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin, and do not say before the angel that it was an error.

note.label: Numbers 30: The Law of Vows

precepts.why:
Solomon carries the law of vows forward: “When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.”

“Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?” Do not let your mouth put your flesh in sin by promising what you will not do, and do not come afterward saying it was an error. A vow that is not paid makes God angry at your voice.

“For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities: but fear thou God.” A fool’s voice is known by multitude of words; the man who fears God does not fill his mouth with vows he cannot keep.

precepts.text: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools: put off the filth learned in this land and drop the prideful rebuttals of the lies you were taught.
precepts.point: Why worship what the Most High created to serve you? The sun, moon, and stars are ordinances that keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept; Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.”

The likeness of beast, fowl, creeping thing and fish were the gods learned in Egypt: Heqet the frog god, Sobek the god of the river, Horus the falcon, the beetles, flies and locusts they deified, and Dagon the fish god of the Babylonians. The sun, moon and stars were Ra and Nut, and today astrology and the zodiac. It was filth learned in Egypt, and this present power is spiritual Egypt and takes after her.

So coming to the house of God, put off the filth learned in this land and drop the prideful rebuttals of the lies you were taught. Be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools, who consider not that they do evil.

precepts.text: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; what comes out of your mouth, be sure to do it.
precepts.point: All the congregation murmured against the princes, but the princes held the line: we have sworn unto them by the LORD God of Israel, now therefore we may not touch them. Our forefathers were wrong in one situation, but they were upright men in holding up to their word.

note.label: Joshua 9: The Gibeonite Deception and the Weight of an Oath

precepts.why:
The princes were deceived, yet when all the congregation murmured they held the line: “We have sworn unto them by the Lord God of Israel: now therefore we may not touch them.” “When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.”

“Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error”. The princes could have said the oath was an error, but they did not; what comes out of your mouth, be sure to do it, lest God be angry at thy voice and destroy the work of thine hands. Our forefathers were wrong in one situation, but they were upright men in holding up to their word.

precepts.text: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay. The angel before whom you must not say it was an error is your personal angel, your guardian angel for lack of a better word, that watches over you and listens to you; do not say, I did not mean to say that. Yes you did; the angel recorded it and knew exactly what it was.
precepts.point: She said to Eli, I am the woman that stood by thee here, praying unto the Lord. For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition which I asked of him: therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord. That is great faith right there that Hannah had, and she kept her promise: Hannah was an upright and honest woman.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

precepts.why:
“When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.”

“Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error”. The angel is your personal angel, your guardian angel for lack of a better word, that watches over you and listens to you. Do not say, I did not mean to say that. Yes you did; the angel recorded it and knew exactly what it was.

Hannah paid her vow. When she had weaned the child she brought him to the house of the Lord in Shiloh and said, “For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition which I asked of him: Therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord.” That is great faith right there, and she kept her promise. Hannah was an upright and honest woman.

precepts.text: If thou seest the oppression of the poor and violent perverting of judgment in a province, marvel not at the matter, for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; what Samuel's sons did is what we see today.
precepts.point: When Samuel was old he made his sons judges over Israel: Joel the firstborn and Abiah his second, judges in Beersheba. But his sons walked not in his ways; they turned aside after lucre, took bribes, and perverted judgment.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.”

What Samuel's sons did, turning aside after lucre, taking bribes and perverting judgment, is what we see today. Do not marvel at it. The Most High, higher than the highest, regards it all.

precepts.text: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it, for he hath no pleasure in fools; better it is that thou shouldest not vow than that thou shouldest vow and not pay, and say not before the angel that it was an error.
precepts.point: The lesson the Most High is teaching Israel here is to pay what you vow. Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay; Saul went back on his word after he had given his yea to the Amorites, and the whole house paid for it.

note.label: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant

precepts.why:
“When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.” And “neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error”.

That is the lesson of the famine. It lasted “three years, year after year”, and when David enquired, “the Lord answered, It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites.” The Gibeonites “were not of the children of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sworn unto them”, yet Saul sought to slay them in his zeal. Saul broke his word.

David asked, “wherewith shall I make the atonement, that ye may bless the inheritance of the Lord?” The blessing was not truly coming from the Gibeonites; it was coming from the Most High, who was teaching Israel a lesson through this famine. They would have “no silver nor gold of Saul, nor of his house”, but asked for seven of his sons to hang up unto the Lord in Gibeah of Saul. Saul did not pay what was vowed, and the whole house paid for it.

precepts.text: See the violent perverting of judgment; marvel not, for there is one higher than they, over how they shoot us down in the streets.
precepts.point: Blessed is the people that know the joyful sound; they shall walk in the light of His countenance. We are going to walk in the laws and be before the Lord blameless like Abraham and our forefathers were.

note.label: Psalm 89: The Covenant Made with David

precepts.why:
Justice and judgment are the habitation of his throne, but on the earth we see the opposite. Solomon says, “If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.”

See the violent perverting of judgment and marvel not, for there is one higher than they. That is over how they shoot us down in the streets. The judges of this province pervert justice, but he that is higher than the highest regards it.

That is why “Blessed is the people that know the joyful sound: they shall walk, O Lord, in the light of thy countenance.” We are going to walk in the laws and be before the Lord blameless like Abraham and our forefathers were, because the Lord is our defence and the Holy One of Israel is our king, higher than all of them.

precepts.text: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God; keep other doctrines away, for the sacrifice of fools is evil.
precepts.point: Holy means severed. We were severed from other people, given a set of laws contrary to all nations. Once we mingle with the other nations we become unholy.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.” When we go into his tabernacles to worship at his footstool, we keep our foot: keep other doctrines away, for the sacrifice of fools is evil. We come to hear his laws and be holy.

precepts.text: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them; the owner only beholds them with his eyes.
precepts.point: Wealth makes many friends, but the poor is separated from his neighbor. When goods increase, so do those that eat them.

note.label: Proverbs 19: Discipline, the Fear of the Lord, and Servitude

precepts.why:
“Wealth maketh many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour.” Money draws a crowd, and the poor man is left by himself.

Solomon says why the crowd comes: “When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good is there to the owners thereof, saving the beholding of them with their eyes?” The more a man has, the more mouths gather to eat it, and the owner himself gets nothing out of it but to look on with his eyes.

Those many friends that wealth makes are the ones increased to eat the goods. That is the friendship riches buy, and it is why the poor man walking in his integrity is better off than the perverse fool with a crowd around him.

precepts.text: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much.
precepts.point: He that blesses his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him. You may have worked fourteen or sixteen hours and are trying to get the last few winks before punching the clock, and a friend calling, texting, or banging on the door early breaks that sweet sleep. Ecclesiastes says the sleep of a laboring man is sweet.

note.label: Proverbs 27: Boast Not of Tomorrow

precepts.why:
“He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.” You may have worked fourteen or sixteen hours and are trying to get the last few winks before punching the clock, and a friend calling, texting, or banging on the door early breaks that sweet sleep. His blessing is a curse to you.

Solomon says what that sleep is worth: “The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.” The laboring man's sleep is sweet whether he ate little or much, and the friend with the loud voice at daybreak is taking it from him.

precepts.text: Christ's warning that men give account of every idle word, matching Solomon's charge to let your words be few.
precepts.point: Be not rash with your mouth nor let your heart be hasty to utter anything before the Most High, for he is in heaven and you upon earth; therefore let your words be few. This means watch your mouth, which is why Christ said you will give account of every word.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.”

Solomon says “Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.” This means watch your mouth, which is why Christ said you will give account of every word. Every idle word is accounted for in the day of judgment, so let your words be few, and be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools, for “a fool’s voice is known by multitude of words.”

precepts.text: Christ's command to swear not at all, by heaven, earth, or your head, which Solomon's warning about vows supports.
precepts.point: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, nor say before the angel that it was an error, lest the Most High be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands. This is what Christ meant by not swearing by heaven, earth, or your own head.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God’s throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.”

This is what Christ meant by not swearing by heaven, earth or your own head, and Solomon's warning about vows supports it: “When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools”, and “Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.” Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, nor say before the angel that it was an error, lest the Most High be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands. Better not to swear at all; but fear the Most High.

precepts.text: Vengeance is the Most High's and he will repay, the assurance Solomon gives against successful wicked men.
precepts.point: Do not worry about the wicked that are successful and all they are doing, because there is a God and that God will have his vengeance. This is why the scriptures say vengeance is his and he will repay.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

precepts.why:
“Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.”

Solomon says when you see the oppression of the poor and the perverting of judgment and justice in a province, “marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.” Do not worry about the wicked that are successful and all they are doing, because there is a God and that God will have his vengeance. Vengeance is his and he will repay; that is the assurance against successful wicked men.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God”: the house of God is the congregation. The Lord told Moses to take the shoes off his feet; he didn’t want Egyptian doctrine tracked up the holy mountain. Don’t track the philosophies you learned into the house of God. “And be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools”: you can’t learn if your mouth is always open. “Therefore let thy words be few.” “When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it.” “Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.” “Neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error”: this all goes back to why Christ told us not to make vows. Angels can, because they fulfil their word.

moments.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

points: If thou seest the oppression of the poor. So if you see the oppression — and here's the thing, you may say, well, they live in a nice house, drive nice cars, they're not poor. Can I get that in Isaiah 14? I think it's like the last verse. If you see the oppression of the poor doesn't necessarily mean financially poor.

And violent perverting of judgment. Now this is a violent perverting of justice. In the times of old, in the 1930s, 1920s, and from whenever they started documenting lynchings, there's always been a violent perverting of judgment. Those coroner reports that we were talking about, those medical examiners, those are violent perversions of justice, because someone should be serving for those hangings, for those drownings, and people are getting off scot-free.

And justice in a province. In a province, in a county, in a state. Can you Google province? A province is a regional administrative division or piece of land inside a country. It is very similar to a state, county or district. Okay. So we're dealing with Ocean Springs, Mississippi. Mississippi being the state, Ocean Springs being a city in the county.
Marvel not at the matter. The Bible says, don't be shocked. You see how they're perverting justice, perverting judgment, perverting evidence. God says, don't be shocked by that.

For he that is higher than the highest regardeth, and there be higher than they. Meaning God is paying attention to this. God is keeping a watchful eye, because there might be some things that we miss. God ain't missing nothing. He sees every hiding of evidence. He sees the perverting of judgment. He sees who's on the payroll, cause now one of the sons' fathers just offered a fifty thousand dollar reward to find the person that did this. Um, sir, it was your son. Ta-da. Send me my money. Case closed. How about that? Hey, I want my check, devil. We got places to go. We got twelve tribes to wake up. Send the check. Case solved.

note.label: Strange Fruit

points: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools. I heard a pastor say that verse means take your shoes off before you go inside the church. That is not what that verse is talking about.

When the Most High called Moses, he told Moses, take your shoes off, for where you stand is holy ground. The shoes represent all the philosophy Moses learned in Egypt. Moses grew up in the house of Pharaoh and learned all the religions and philosophies; they were worshipping a lot of gods. The Most High said, do not come in here with that same mindset. That's what keep thy foot means: do not come here with that trash you learned in the Christian churches. Whatever you learned, you got to start all over again.

That's why Christ said you must come as little children. Little children are ready to learn; you can teach little children anything. How does the saying go? It is easier to raise strong children than to repair broken men. And let me tell you, some of us are broken. We are a broken people.

A word to the young sisters: there are consequences for everything you do in life. Do not think you can go out there and do certain things and it's not going to come back later. And understand what wins a man: it is not the degree, the career, or the money; men care about respect and loyalty. Guard yourself accordingly.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

points: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
Let your words be few. Control your mouth. There's a time and a place for everything. Be mindful of what you say, be mindful of the things you say to people, and the things you take in as well.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: If thou seest the oppression of the poor and violent perverting of judgment, marvel not, for he that is higher than the highest regardeth: America blockaded Cuba and Venezuela, kidnapped Maduro, and babies are dying on ventilators with no power while Europe and the Philippines said nothing. So the Lord flipped it: Iran blocked the strait and starved the world's oil, and now Europe calls it a crisis.

note.label: Trump Is Fulfilling God's Prophecy

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

points: Be not rash with your mouth nor let your heart be hasty to utter anything before the Most High, for he is in heaven and you upon earth; therefore let your words be few. This means watch your mouth, which is why Christ said you will give account of every word.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

points: A dream comes through the multitude of business and a fool's voice through a multitude of words. Dreams come through what you are doing: if you play games all day you may dream of it, and if you teach all the time you may dream you are still teaching.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

points: When you vow a vow to the Most High, do not defer to pay it, for he has no pleasure in fools; it is better not to vow than to vow and not pay.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

points: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, nor say before the angel that it was an error, lest the Most High be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands. This is what Christ meant by not swearing by heaven, earth, or your own head.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

points: In the multitude of dreams and many words there are also diverse vanities, but fear the Most High.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

points: If you see the oppression of the poor and the perverting of judgment and justice in a province, do not marvel, for he that is higher than the highest regards it, and there are higher than they.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

points: He that loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver, nor he that loves abundance with increase; this also is vanity. When goods increase, those that eat them increase.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

points: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of the rich will not let him sleep. The rich lose sleep to gain wealth; ask successful entrepreneurs and businessmen and they work off four or five hours of sleep.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

points: There is a sore evil under the sun: riches kept for the owners to their hurt, and those riches perish by evil travail so that the son is left with nothing in his hand.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

points: As a man came from his mother's womb naked, so shall he return, and take nothing of his labor to carry away in his hand. In all points as he came, so shall he go, and he has labored for the wind, eating in darkness with much sorrow, wrath, and sickness.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

points: It is good and comely for a man to eat, drink, and enjoy the good of all his labor all the days of his life which the Most High gives him, for it is his portion.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 5: Vows, Riches, and the Gift of God

points: Every man to whom the Most High gives riches, wealth, and power to enjoy them and rejoice in his labor, this is the gift of the Most High. He shall not much remember the days of his life, because the Most High answers him in the joy of his heart.
